subject: General Knowledge
topic: Martial Arts of India — Regional Forms and Traditions
description: Covers India's major indigenous martial art forms — Kalaripayattu, Gatka, Thang-ta, Silambam, Mardani Khel, Chhau — their states, community associations, weapons, and UNESCO status.

questions.stem: Which Indian martial art, native to Kerala, is widely regarded as one of the world's oldest surviving martial arts and includes a unique flexible sword called the urumi in its advanced weapon curriculum?

options.option_text: Kalaripayattu — body-to-weapon progression in three stages: meithari, kolthari, ankathari
Gatka — Sikh martial tradition using swords, staves, and the khanda
Thang-ta — Manipuri sword-and-spear system of the Meitei warriors
Silambam — Tamil Nadu's bamboo staff martial art of Sangam antiquity

questions.explanation: KALARIPAYATTU (Kerala): One of the world's oldest martial arts, traceable to at least the 3rd century BCE. Name means 'practice in the kalari (training ground).' THREE TRAINING STAGES: (1) MEITHARI — body exercises, kicks, jumps, flexibility drills. (2) KOLTHARI — wooden weapon combat (staves, short sticks). (3) ANKATHARI — metal weapon combat (sword, shield, spear, dagger, urumi). THE URUMI (whip-sword): A flexible metal strip used as both sword and whip — the most dangerous weapon in Kalaripayattu, requiring years to master. TWO REGIONAL STYLES: Northern (Vadakkan) — higher kicks, more acrobatic; Southern (Thekkan) — lower stances, emphasis on strikes. COLONIAL SUPPRESSION: Arms Act 1878 drove weapon-based practice underground. POST-INDEPENDENCE REVIVAL: Now practiced by both Hindu and Muslim communities (Muslim variant: Chaverpada). UPSC ANGLE: Many scholars believe Kalaripayattu influenced Asian martial arts via Buddhist monks who trained in Kerala before traveling to China/Southeast Asia — but this connection is debated. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims GS-1 Culture, KPSC, NDA GK.

questions.stem: Gatka, the traditional armed martial art of the Sikh community, is most closely associated with which warrior order and which annual festival where it is prominently displayed?

options.option_text: Nihang warriors — displayed at Hola Mohalla festival at Anandpur Sahib, Punjab
Akali warriors — displayed at Baisakhi celebrations at the Golden Temple, Amritsar
Sevadars — displayed at Gurpurab (Guru Nanak Jayanti) across all major Gurudwaras
Granthis — displayed at Diwali (Bandi Chhor Divas) at Hazur Sahib, Nanded

questions.explanation: GATKA: Traditional Sikh martial art linked to shastar vidiya (science of weapons). NIHANG WARRIORS: A distinct Sikh warrior order identifiable by blue robes, tall turbans topped with the CHAKAR (circular steel throwing weapon), and the KHANDA (double-edged sword). They are the primary custodians of Gatka in its combat form. HOLA MOHALLA: A Sikh festival instituted by Guru Gobind Singh as a martial festival — held the day after Holi at ANANDPUR SAHIB (Punjab). Features: mock battles, Gatka demonstrations, horse riding, archery. It is the PREMIER display occasion for Gatka nationwide. WEAPONS IN GATKA: (1) LATHI (bamboo staff — introductory). (2) KIRPAN (sword). (3) TALWAR (curved sword). (4) KHANDA (double-edged — on the Nishan Sahib flag). (5) SHIELD (dhal). HISTORICAL ORIGIN: Guru Hargobind Sahib (6th Guru) introduced Miri-Piri doctrine and built Akal Takht — formalizing temporal/martial identity alongside spiritual. COMMON TRAP: Baisakhi celebrates the founding of the Khalsa (1699) and features Gatka too, but HOLA MOHALLA is specifically the martial arts festival. MEMORY AID: 'HOLA + MOHALLA = HOLE (drill/practice) in MOHALLA (locality) — a military drill festival.' PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, UPSC Prelims GS-1, PPSC (Punjab PSC).

questions.stem: Thang-ta (Huyen Langlon) is Manipur's traditional armed martial art. Which of the following CORRECTLY describes its two components and the community that practices it?

options.option_text: Practiced by the Meitei people — Thang-ta (sword-spear combat) and Sarit Sarak (unarmed combat) are the two components
Practiced by the Naga community — Thang-ta (staff combat) and Mukna (wrestling) are the two components
Practiced by the Kuki-Zo people — Thang-ta (knife combat) and Inbuan (grappling) are the two components
Practiced by the Mizo community — Thang-ta (spear dance) and Cheraw (bamboo dance combat) are the two components

questions.explanation: THANG-TA (Huyen Langlon): THANG = sword, TA = spear — the traditional martial system of the MEITEI people of Manipur, historically the warrior class of the Manipur Kingdom. TWO COMPONENTS: (1) THANG-TA: The armed combat system using swords (thang), spears (ta), shields, and other metal weapons. (2) SARIT SARAK: The UNARMED combat component — strikes, joint locks, throws, grappling techniques. HISTORICAL CONTEXT: Used by the royal palace guards (Lallup-Kaba system) of the Manipur Kingdom. SUPPRESSION: The British suppressed Thang-ta after the Anglo-Manipuri War (1891) as a tool of resistance. SURVIVAL: Preserved within families and through integration into MEITEI cultural festivals — particularly the LAI HARAOBA (invoking the old gods) festival where Thang-ta movements are incorporated into ritual dance. RECOGNITION: Recognized by Sangeet Natak Akademi as a classical martial art form. DISTINGUISH FROM: MUKNA = Manipuri traditional wrestling (unarmed, practiced by Meitei males, held at Mera Houchongba festival). CHERAW = Mizoram's bamboo dance (not martial). INBUAN = Mizoram's traditional wrestling. MEMORY AID: 'THANG-TA = Sword-Spear, the MEITEI warrior's twin tools.' PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-1, MPSC, NDA GK, CDS.

questions.stem: Silambam, Tamil Nadu's ancient bamboo staff martial art, places great emphasis on footwork as the foundation of training. What is distinctive about the Silambam staff length, and which ancient literary work mentions this art?

options.option_text: Staff of 1.68 metres (just above head height) — mentioned in the Silappatikaram, one of the Five Great Tamil Epics (2nd century CE)
Staff of the practitioner's exact body height — mentioned in the Thirukkural, the Tamil ethical treatise by Tiruvalluvar
Staff of 3 metres (two body lengths) — mentioned in the Manimekalai, the Tamil Buddhist epic of Merchant Kovalan
Staff of half the practitioner's height — mentioned in the Tolkappiyam, the ancient Tamil grammar treatise

questions.explanation: SILAMBAM STAFF SPECIFICATIONS: The combat staff (silambam kol) is standardised at 1.68 METRES — slightly above the average practitioner's head height. This ensures the staff can function as both an offensive and defensive tool — the extra length above the head creates a striking arc that attackers must account for. TRAINING PROGRESSION: Students begin with a staff of their OWN HEIGHT before graduating to the 1.68m combat staff — teaching correct proportional handling before adding reach. LITERARY EVIDENCE — SILAPPATIKARAM ('The Tale of the Anklet'): Written by Ilango Adigal (Prince of the Chera dynasty), c. 2nd century CE. One of the Five Great Tamil Epics (Pancha Maha Kavyam). Mentions 'Silambattam' as an established warrior art and sport of the Tamil kingdoms. This is one of the earliest literary references to a codified martial art in South India. CURRICULUM STRUCTURE: (1) FOOTWORK PATTERNS — 12 basic foot movements (the absolute foundation). (2) BASIC STRIKES — offensive techniques. (3) DEFENSIVE BLOCKS. (4) ANIMAL FORMS — snake, eagle, tiger-inspired movements. (5) MULTI-WEAPON — sword, knife, dual staves in advanced training. COMMON TRAP: The Thirukkural is an ethical treatise, NOT a martial arts text. Silappatikaram is the correct source. MEMORY AID: '1.68m = just above your head — Silambam keeps enemies at HEAD level away.' PYQ FREQUENCY: TNPSC (very high), SSC CGL, UPSC GS-1 Culture.

questions.stem: Mardani Khel is the traditional close-combat martial art of the Maratha warriors. Which distinctive weapon, worn as a glove with a long blade extending from it, is uniquely associated with this tradition?

options.option_text: Patta (gauntlet sword) — a basket-hilted blade worn over the hand, allowing simultaneous dual-weapon use
Urumi (whip-sword) — a flexible metal blade used both as a sword and as a whip for mid-range combat
Khanda (double-edged sword) — a straight-bladed weapon used by Rajput and Sikh warriors
Talwar (curved sword) — the standard curved cavalry sword of the Mughal-era armies

questions.explanation: MARDANI KHEL: Traditional armed combat system of the MARATHA WARRIORS of Maharashtra. 'Mardani' = manly/warrior-like; 'Khel' = sport/play. Developed under the MARATHA EMPIRE, particularly associated with CHHATRAPATI SHIVAJI MAHARAJ's guerrilla tradition in the Sahyadri (Western Ghats). THE PATTA (GAUNTLET SWORD): The defining weapon of Mardani Khel. Structure: A basket-hilt encases the entire fist → a long straight or slightly curved blade extends from it, rigidly attached. The HAND IS INSIDE THE HILT — the sword becomes an extension of the arm, not a held object. Advantage: (1) Cannot be disarmed. (2) Both hands can wield a patta simultaneously. (3) Particularly effective in the confined spaces of hill forts and narrow passes. The Maratha emphasis on hill-fort (gadh) warfare made compact, irremovable weapons essential. OTHER MARDANI KHEL WEAPONS: VITA (weighted rope dart — thrown and retracted), DANDPATTA (two-handed patta variant), LEZIM (rhythmic training tool). DISTINGUISH: URUMI = Kerala's Kalaripayattu flexible sword. KHANDA = Sikh/Rajput double-edged sword. TALWAR = Mughal cavalry curved sword. MEMORY AID: 'Patta = PAT on the back of the hand — literally strapped to the hand.' UPSC ANGLE: Maratha weapons reflect the unique Deccan terrain — compact, efficient for hill warfare rather than open-field cavalry combat. PYQ FREQUENCY: MPSC (Maharashtra PSC — very high), SSC CGL, NDA GK.

questions.stem: Chhau dance-martial art has three regional variants inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010. Which variant is the ONLY one that does NOT use a mask, relying instead on facial expressions for character portrayal?

options.option_text: Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha) — uses facial abhinaya (expression) instead of masks
Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand) — uses symbolic abstract masks but retains some facial expression
Purulia Chhau (West Bengal) — the most acrobatic form, uses minimal masks for acrobatic freedom
All three variants use masks — the difference lies only in the material and colour of the masks

questions.explanation:
CHHAU — THREE VARIANTS and their KEY DIFFERENCES:
→ SERAIKELLA CHHAU (Jharkhand, formerly Bihar): Uses ELABORATE MASKS — papier-mâché and clay-based, stylised and abstract. Storylines from Ramayana, Mahabharata, Puranas. Patronised by the royal family of Seraikella kingdom.
→ PURULIA CHHAU (West Bengal): Uses the most COLOURFUL, STRIKING MASKS — large, exaggerated features. Most acrobatic form — high jumps, spins, martial flips. Most widely performed outside home states.
→ MAYURBHANJ CHHAU (Odisha): The ONLY MASKLESS variant — relies entirely on ABHINAYA (facial expressions, body language) for character portrayal. Considered the most 'classical' in technique. Named after Mayurbhanj district of Odisha.
MASK-MAKING TRADITIONS: Purulia masks = papier-mâché (easily made, colourful). Seraikella masks = more refined, often clay + papier-mâché. Mayurbhanj = NO masks.
UNESCO INSCRIPTION: All three variants were inscribed TOGETHER on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.
CHHAU vs KALARIPAYATTU: Chhau = martial-dance synthesis, primarily ritual/theatrical. Kalaripayattu = combat art with performance elements.
MEMORY AID: 'May-URB-hanj = URBane without a mask — the refined, maskless form.' 'PURUlia = PURE acrobatics.' 'SERAIkella = SEALED behind a mask.'
PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-1 Culture (very high), SSC CGL, WBPSC, OPSC.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court of India's landmark order in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1996) regarding the Taj Mahal directly relates to which environmental threat also relevant to Indian martial arts heritage sites?

options.option_text: Acid rain from sulphur dioxide emissions by the Mathura Refinery, dissolving the marble of the Taj Mahal through 'marble cancer'
Rising groundwater due to irrigation canals, causing subsidence of the Taj Mahal's foundations
Vibrations from heavy vehicular traffic on the Agra-Delhi highway, weakening the Taj Mahal's structural integrity
Uncontrolled tourism causing surface erosion of the Taj Mahal's marble through repeated foot traffic

questions.explanation: M.C. MEHTA v. UNION OF INDIA (1996) — TAJ TRAPEZIUM ZONE CASE: A landmark PIL (Public Interest Litigation) filed by environmental lawyer M.C. Mehta before the Supreme Court of India. ISSUE: The MATHURA OIL REFINERY (established 1975, ~40 km from Agra) was emitting SULPHUR DIOXIDE (SO₂). SO₂ + atmospheric moisture → SULPHURIC ACID → 'ACID RAIN' → fell on the Taj Mahal → reacted with its WHITE MARBLE (calcium carbonate, CaCO₃): CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ (gypsum, soft and crumbly) + H₂O + CO₂. This is called 'MARBLE CANCER' — the surface becomes soft, powdery, and yellowish-brown. THE TAJ TRAPEZIUM ZONE (TTZ): The Supreme Court directed that: (1) Industries within the 10,400 sq km TTZ around Agra must shift from coal to natural gas or relocate. (2) Mathura Refinery must install sulphur scrubbers. (3) No new polluting industry within the TTZ. RELEVANCE TO MARTIAL ARTS: Many historical sites where martial arts were practiced (fort complexes, temple grounds — especially stone-carved structures) face the same acid rain threat. Red Fort (sandstone), Fatehpur Sikri — all in the Agra-Mathura belt. UPSC ANGLE: This case is simultaneously: (1) A landmark in PIL evolution (locus standi expansion). (2) A landmark in environmental jurisprudence (polluter pays principle applied). (3) Evidence for the 'precautionary principle' in Supreme Court jurisprudence. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims GS-2 (Polity — PIL, SC landmark cases), GS-3 (Environment — acid rain, pollution), SSC CGL, CLAT.

questions.stem: Mallakhamb, the traditional pole-gymnastics martial discipline, was officially declared the State Sport by which Indian state in the year 2013?

options.option_text: Maharashtra — where Mallakhamb was historically revived
Madhya Pradesh — it declared Mallakhamb state sport in 2013
Gujarat — frequent host of National Mallakhamb Championship
Rajasthan — home to numerous traditional akharas and wrestlers

questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh officially declared Mallakhamb as its State Sport in 2013, becoming the first state to grant this recognition to the discipline. Maharashtra is the most common wrong choice because Mallakhamb was revived and popularised there during the 19th century by Balambhatta Dada Deodhar, but the official State Sport declaration belongs to Madhya Pradesh.

questions.stem: The Paika Akhada of Odisha trained the warrior community in traditional armed combat. In which year did Paika fighters, led by Bakshi Jagabandhu, launch their rebellion against British colonial rule — now recognised as one of India's earliest armed uprisings?

options.option_text: 1799 — year of Tipu Sultan's defeat at the Battle of Seringapatam
1817 — the Paika Bidroha that predated the 1857 Sepoy Mutiny
1831 — year of the Wahabi-inspired Barasat Uprising in Bengal
1857 — the pan-India First War of Independence against the British

questions.explanation: The Paika Bidroha of 1817 was led by Bakshi Jagabandhu against the British East India Company in Odisha. In 2017, on its 200th anniversary, the Government of India officially recognised it as the first major armed uprising against British rule — predating the famous 1857 revolt by four decades. The year 1857 is the most tempting distractor as it is canonically taught as the first war of independence.

questions.stem: Thoda is a traditional Himalayan martial art-festival combining archery with group mock combat between two teams called 'Pashis' and 'Shauthis', both rooted in Mahabharata lore. It is celebrated primarily during Baisakhi in which Indian state?

options.option_text: Uttarakhand — celebrated during Garhwali folk festivals annually
Himachal Pradesh — Thoda is performed in Shimla and Sirmour areas
Sikkim — practiced alongside Losoong and Namsoong celebrations
Manipur — home to several ancient archery and combat traditions

questions.explanation: Thoda is native to Himachal Pradesh, practiced mainly in the Shimla and Sirmour districts during Baisakhi. The two competing teams — Pashis and Shauthis — represent the Pandavas and Kauravas respectively, anchoring the sport in Mahabharata tradition. Uttarakhand is a tempting distractor due to cultural and geographic proximity to Himachal, but Thoda is specifically a Himachali martial tradition.

questions.stem: Musti Yuddha, an ancient form of Indian bare-knuckle combat that incorporates strikes, knee attacks, and grappling, is most closely associated with the traditional akhadas (wrestling arenas) of which Indian city?

options.option_text: Prayagraj — site of historic Kumbh Mela wrestling competitions
Varanasi — where traditional akhadas have preserved Musti Yuddha
Mathura — linked to Lord Krishna's legendary wrestling exploits
Ayodhya — associated with Ramayana-era martial training traditions

questions.explanation: Musti Yuddha has been continuously preserved in the traditional akhadas of Varanasi (Kashi), which remains the primary living centre for this ancient combat art. Mathura is the classic wrong choice due to its association with Krishna's famous wrestling in the Mahabharata, but that refers to Malla Yuddha (grappling/wrestling), not specifically Musti Yuddha, and Mathura's tradition is tied to mythology rather than a surviving martial school.

questions.stem: Inbuan wrestling, the traditional martial sport of Mizoram, has a highly distinctive physical constraint that sets it apart from virtually all other Indian wrestling disciplines. Which of the following is that defining rule?

options.option_text: Competitors must grip each other's belt and never release the hold
Bending the knees at any point during the bout is strictly forbidden
Bouts are conducted inside an earthen pit, not on a raised platform
Victory requires lifting the opponent completely above shoulder height

questions.explanation: In Inbuan wrestling, competitors must maintain a completely upright stance — bending the knees is strictly prohibited throughout the bout. Wrestlers grip each other at the waist and attempt throws while keeping both legs rigid. Option A (belt grip) is partially true as a separate rule, but it is not the unique distinguishing feature; the absolute ban on bending the knees is what makes Inbuan unmistakably different from all other regional wrestling forms in India.

questions.stem: The Kalaripayattu gurukul system prescribes a mandatory four-stage progression for students. Which option CORRECTLY lists these four stages in their proper ascending order from foundational to most advanced?

options.option_text: Kolthari → Meithari → Angathari → Verumkai
Meithari → Kolthari → Angathari → Verumkai
Angathari → Meithari → Kolthari → Verumkai
Meithari → Angathari → Kolthari → Verumkai

questions.explanation: The correct progression is: Meithari (body conditioning — flexibility, jumps, stances) → Kolthari (wooden weapons — staff, otta curved stick) → Angathari (metal weapons — sword, shield, spear, dagger) → Verumkai (empty-hand combat against armed opponents — the apex and most advanced stage). The most common exam error is placing Angathari before Kolthari; the pedagogical logic is that students must master safer wooden weapons before advancing to lethal metal ones.

questions.stem: Niyuddha Kridā, the ancient Indian combat sport encompassing wrestling, striking, and grappling, is explicitly listed as one of the Chatushashti Kalas (64 traditional arts) in which classical Sanskrit text?

options.option_text: Kautilya's Arthashastra — the treatise on statecraft and warfare
Vatsyayana's Kamasutra — which catalogues the 64 traditional arts
Charaka Samhita — the foundational Ayurvedic text on medicine
Sushruta Samhita — the classical surgical and anatomical compendium

questions.explanation: Vatsyayana's Kamasutra contains the celebrated list of 64 arts (Chatushashti Kalas) that a cultured person of the classical era was expected to master; Niyuddha Kridā (competitive combat sport) features in this enumeration. Kautilya's Arthashastra is the strongest distractor as it extensively covers military training, army organisation, and statecraft, but it does not enumerate the Chatushashti Kalas — that framework belongs to Vatsyayana.
